title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 217 (Procedure, powers, etc., of inspectors)

content.overview: Section 217 confers on an inspector appointed under the Chapter the powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure in respect of discovery and production of books and documents, summoning and enforcing attendance of persons, examining them on oath, and inspection of books and registers. Officers, employees and agents of the company must preserve and produce books and give assistance. The inspector may examine on oath any person who may be acquainted with the affairs. Notes of examination signed by the person examined may be used in evidence. Failure to produce, answer or assist attracts the penalties stated in the section.
content.glance: Inspector has civil-court powers for discovery, production, attendance and examination on oath; officers/employees/agents must assist; notes of examination usable in evidence; penalties for non-compliance.
content.study: It shall be the duty of all officers and other employees and agents of the company to preserve and produce to an inspector all books and papers of the company and to give the inspector all assistance. An inspector may examine on oath any person who is or has been an officer or employee or agent of the company, or any other person, in relation to the affairs of the company. Notes of any examination shall be taken down in writing and signed by the person examined and may thereafter be used in evidence against him. An inspector shall have the powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure for discovery and production, summoning and enforcing attendance, examining on oath, and inspection of books and registers. Current-law framing: identify the inspector; apply civil-court powers; enforce duty to produce and assist; use signed notes as evidence; apply penalties for failure.

sections.heading: Civil-Court Powers
sections.body: Powers of a civil court for discovery and production, attendance, examination on oath, and inspection of books and registers.

sections.heading: Duty to Assist
sections.body: Officers, employees and agents must preserve and produce books and give all assistance to the inspector.

sections.heading: Examination on Oath
sections.body: Inspector may examine on oath any person acquainted with the affairs; notes signed by the examinee may be used in evidence.

sections.heading: Penalties
sections.body: Failure to produce, answer or assist attracts the consequences the section provides.

examples.title: Examination on oath
examples.body: An inspector summons a former CFO and examines him on oath about related-party transfers. Notes are taken and signed. Under s. 217 those notes may be used in evidence against him.

examples.title: Refusal to produce
examples.body: An officer refuses to produce statutory registers demanded by the inspector. Section 217 imposes a duty to produce and assist; non-compliance attracts the section’s penalties.

hypotheticals.question: Does an inspector need a separate court order for every document production under s. 217?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 217 itself confers civil-court powers of discovery and production on the inspector. The section is the source of the power; a separate production order from a civil court is not required for each demand within that statutory power.

distinctions.title: Powers of inspectors (s. 217) vs conduct of inspection (s. 207)
distinctions.left: Powers of inspectors appointed for investigation (discovery, oath, evidence)
distinctions.right: Duties during Registrar’s inspection/inquiry under s. 206

misconceptions.trap: Notes of examination by an inspector can never be used as evidence.
misconceptions.correction: Section 217 provides that notes of examination taken down in writing and signed by the person examined may be used in evidence against him.

questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm inspector appointment. II. Apply civil-court powers and duty to assist. III. Note examination and evidence use. IV. Apply penalties. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.answer: Inspector status; powers invoked; compliance; precise relief.
